memory_update.text: TOST should remain in the restaurant value/traffic node as a scaled public supplier of POS, direct ordering, loyalty, offers, and guest-data infrastructure.

PAR is below the preferred market-cap threshold in the latest finance snapshot but is a high-relevance exception for QSR/fast-casual POS, loyalty, digital ordering, and enterprise restaurant infrastructure.
MIDD maps to the equipment side of value preservation: throughput, beverage systems, automation, cooking platforms, and daypart/menu-expansion capability.
SYY is a key input-side candidate because the pending Jetro Restaurant Depot transaction directly targets independent restaurants, low-priced products, and cash-and-carry replenishment.
PFGC maps to value-menu and margin-support infrastructure through foodservice distribution, independent/chain case growth, and private-label Performance Brands penetration.

Potentially relevant but not included due to the five-candidate cap: USFD, VYX, SQ/Block, DoorDash, Instacart, Westrock Coffee, Starbucks supplier ecosystem, packaging suppliers, and payment processors. VYX appears especially relevant for Aloha restaurant POS but should be checked separately because its latest market cap snapshot was slightly below $1B.

For this node, the most testable supplier chokepoints are: direct-ordering and loyalty conversion, enterprise POS/menu orchestration, low-cost ingredient sourcing, private-label penetration, cash-and-carry availability, beverage/daypart equipment, and kitchen throughput/labor-saving equipment.

node: Consumer value, traffic, and menu-pricing power
summary: Expanded universe for the value/traffic/menu-pricing node focuses on enabling infrastructure rather than restaurant operators: restaurant POS, loyalty, digital ordering, kitchen/beverage equipment, and broadline distribution/private-label food inputs. The working chokepoint is the ability to protect frequency and perceived value without relying only on menu-price inflation. Candidates are not ranked and are research leads only.
